chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Azineh, from Aban ibn Abi Ayyash, from Sulaym ibn Qays al-Hilaly; and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Yaqub ibn Yazid and Ibrahim ibn Hashim together, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Umar al-Yamani, from Aban ibn Abi Ayyash, from Sulaym ibn Qays al-Hilaly who said: I heard Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Tayyar saying:

We were with Muawiyah, along with Al-Hasan, Al-Husayn, Abdullah ibn Abbas, Umar ibn Abi Salama, and Usama ibn Zayd. An argument occurred between me and Muawiyah, so I said to Muawiyah: 'I heard the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) say: I am closer to the believers than their own selves. Then my brother Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) is closer to the believers than their own selves. When Ali is martyred, then Al-Hasan ibn Ali is closer to the believers than their own selves. Then his son Al-Husayn is next, closer to the believers than their own selves. When he is martyred, then his son Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Akbar is closer to the believers than their own selves. Then my son Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir is closer to the believers than their own selves. You will meet him, O Husayn. Then twelve Imams will complete the line, nine of whom are from the progeny of Husayn (may God be pleased with him).' Abdullah ibn Ja'far said: 'Then Al-Hasan, Al-Husayn, Abdullah ibn Abbas, Umar ibn Abi Salama, and Usama ibn Zayd were martyred, and they testified for me before Muawiyah.' Sulaym ibn Qays al-Hilaly said: 'I also heard this from Salman, Abu Dharr, and Al-Miqdad, and they mentioned that they heard it from the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family).'

key_terms.أَخِي: My brother (referring to Ali ibn Abi Talib)
key_terms.أَوْلَى بِالْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Closer to the believers (referring to authority and guardianship)
key_terms.الْبَاقِرُ: The Bagger (title of the fifth Imam, Muhammad ibn Ali)
key_terms.رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ: May God be pleased with him

ai.seo_question: What is the chain of succession for the Twelve Imams according to Sulaym ibn Qays?
ai.summary: This narration from Sulaym ibn Qays al-Hilaly, a prominent early Shia scholar, records Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Tayyar citing the Prophet’s declaration of Ali’s authority over the believers during a debate with Muawiyah. The text outlines the succession of the Twelve Imams, starting with Ali, then Hasan, Husayn, Ali ibn al-Husayn, Muhammad al-Baqir, and concluding with the twelve Imams, nine of whom are from the progeny of Husayn. It serves as a key text for the doctrine of Imamate and the virtues of the Ahl al-Bayt.
